summary: This diff adds a new, self-contained src/lib/prompt-compiler/ TypeScript module (Layer 2-5 compiler pipeline: entity/variable extraction, multi-level intent classification, context assembly, prompt construction/hashing/fingerprinting, confidence scoring, verification) plus Intelligence/Matching engines (similarity, ranking/recommendation, optimizer/expansion, portability, A/B testing, testing/benchmark), a small additive extension to capability-registry-service.ts (new prompt_version entity type mirroring the existing prompt_pattern/dynamic_chain pattern, with correctly updated tests), and a smoke-test script. Every pipeline stage is pure and deterministic with no LLM calls, no new DB tables/migrations, and no changes to auth, schema, or API routes -- nothing here is wired into a live route yet, so blast radius is effectively zero. Verified no eval/child_process/raw-SQL/secrets in the new code, the capability-registry-service.ts extension correctly reuses existing org-scoped embedding storage (storeEmbedding/findSimilar with orgId) rather than bypassing multi-tenant scoping, and the persist-compiled-prompt.ts DB write path delegates auth/permission enforcement entirely to phase_1's existing createPromptVersion (no new auth surface introduced). ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml and PROGRESS.md accurately reflect the actual code changes. This is additive, isolated, well-tested library code with no schema/auth/migration/workflow-file changes, matching tier1 criteria cleanly.
issues: Minor doc/code mismatch in prompt-ranking-recommendation.ts's recommendRelatedTemplates: the comment claims duplicate templateKey entries get 'summed strength' but the merge logic (line ~102) actually just keeps whichever entry has the higher strength, discarding the other rather than summing. Cosmetic only -- this function has no callers yet in this diff.

The Layer 5 verification pipeline's permission/business-rule checks (verification-pipeline.ts) are advisory only (populate an allPassed flag) and are not enforced by any caller in this diff, since no API route consumes this pipeline yet -- expected per this phase's own stated scope (enforcement is future work), just flagging that no route currently depends on or bypasses this check.
